title: Corey and Her Coriander Mints
style: warm acoustic folk, 78 BPM, nylon guitar, light hand percussion, gentle upright bass, warm female lead vocal with soft male harmony, multilingual passing phrases english spanish, curious storyteller tone, kitchen-table intimacy, world-folk influence, no auto-tune, no edm, no aggressive production
lyrics:
[Intro — gentle, curious]
Corey and her coriander mints
Mint with watermelon, who would have thought
A little leaf, a little sweet
A little something the world forgot

[Verse 1]
Cilantro in the south, coriander in the north
Same green leaf, two names going forth
In Spanish it's cilantro, en español, cilantro
In English coriander, slow it down, let it grow
Mint is menta, watermelon is sandía
Sandía con menta, una sorpresa del día

[Chorus]
Corey and her coriander mints
Little bites of culture, little hints
Maybe red onion, maybe not
Taste it slow and see what you got
Mint and watermelon, easy yummy
Food is language, food is family

[Verse 2]
In Vietnam they call it rau mùi, soft on the tongue
In India it's dhania, the cooks have always sung
In Arabic it's kuzbara, in the markets warm and bright
Every kitchen has a name, every name has a light
Not all of us know, and that is okay
We taste, we ask, we learn the way

[Bridge — half-spoken, warm]
I think it's red onion, maybe
Mint and watermelon, easy
A little salt, a little lime
A little patience, a little time
The old ways carry the answers
The new tongues carry them home
Three three six

[Chorus 2]
Corey and her coriander mints
Little bites of culture, little hints
Maybe red onion, maybe not
Taste it slow and see what you got
Mint and watermelon, easy yummy
Food is language, food is family

[Outro — gentle]
Cilantro, menta, sandía
Coriander, mint, watermelon
Thank the hands that grew it
Thank the tongues that named it
Corey and her coriander mints
